title: Because sin is not small… and love is not cheap.
paragraphs: Because sin is not small… and love is not cheap.
Let me say it straight, kapatid—

If God could just “ignore” sin and save humanity anyway…
then justice would be a lie.
And love would be shallow.
From the beginning, Scripture draws a hard line:
“The wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23

Not discomfort.
Not a warning.
Death.
Why?

Because sin is not just a mistake.
It’s rebellion against a holy God.
It’s choosing self over the Source of life.
And when you disconnect from Life…
you get death.
So why blood?
Because in the Bible, blood represents life.
“For the life of the flesh is in the blood…” — Leviticus 17:11
Life had to answer for the loss of life.

Not because God is cruel—
but because God is just.
Here’s the tension most people miss:

God is holy…
and God is love.
So what happens when sinful humanity stands before a holy God?
Judgment is deserved.
But mercy is desired.
And that’s where everything shifts.

Not with an excuse.
Not with a loophole.
But with a sacrifice.

In the Old Testament, animals were offered—
temporary coverings for sin.
But those sacrifices were never the final answer.
They were shadows.
Pointing forward.
Waiting.
Then comes Jesus.

Not just a teacher.
Not just a prophet.
The Lamb.
“Behold, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.” — John 1:29
And here’s the scandal of grace:
God didn’t demand your blood.
He gave His own.

Jesus lived the life we couldn’t live—
perfect, spotless.

Then died the death we deserved—
brutal, unjust, bloody.
Why blood?

Because forgiveness is not free—
it is paid for.
“Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.” — Hebrews 9:22
But hear this clearly:
God didn’t require blood from you to crush you.
He provided blood for you to save you.
The cross is where justice and mercy kissed.

Sin was punished.
But the sinner was offered grace.
So no—God couldn’t just “save humanity” by ignoring sin.

That would mean evil wins.
That would mean righteousness bends.
But instead—
Jesus stepped in.

Took the weight.
Spilled the blood.
Opened the way.
And now the invitation stands:
Not “be perfect.”
Not “earn it.”
But—
repent and believe.

Turn from sin.
Trust in Christ.
Receive what was paid in full.
This is not just theology.
This is rescue.

From scandal to grace—
because Jesus rewrites everything.
